pages.text: Energy Cells are your grid's $(4)reservoir$(0): they decouple generation from consumption, so a stuttering generator never starves your machines.$(br2)$(bold)Basic Cell:$(0)$(li)Capacity: $(bold)500 million$(0) AE$(li)Up to $(4)1 million AE/tick$(0) in or out (shared charge/discharge limit)$(br2)Tier comparison on the next page. Pro tip: drop a Portable Cell into its charge slot and the cell tops it up for you.

$(bold)Three tiers of storage$(0) (capacity / per-tick transfer):$(li)$(4)Basic$(0): 500 million / 1 million$(li)Advanced: 2 billion / 5 million$(li)$(4)Super$(0): 20 billion / 50 million$(br2)Advanced and Super are crafted by upgrading the tier below them, and tiers mix freely in one grid.$(br2)That transfer limit decides your burst throughput — when your generators and pipes are fast, don't let a small cell become the bottleneck.$(br2)One cell not enough? See the "$(l:akaishi:cell_serializer)Cell Serializer$(/l)" for a mega-battery.

Storing is only half the job: get started with "$(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l)", then pair the "$(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l)" or "$(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Generator Matrix$(/l)" with "$(l:akaishi:energy_pipe)Energy Pipes$(/l)" into a full loop — scale up with the "$(l:akaishi:cell_serializer)Cell Serializer$(/l)" and carry "$(l:akaishi:portable_cell)Portable Cells$(/l)" when you head out.
